claim: Microsoft AI has published an explicit chain-of-command and human-control specification, creating a concrete benchmark for executable agent authority and evaluation controls.
verifiedFacts: Microsoft AI published a draft Humanist AI Code of Conduct on September 14, 2026 and opened a six-week public consultation.
The document defines Users and Operators, a Chain of Command, Human Control Requirements, absolute constraints, transparency requirements, and a future evaluation program.
Microsoft states the draft is not yet used to train current models and is not a guarantee of present model behavior.
inference: The market is moving from broad AI principles toward inspectable role, authority, interruption, traceability, and evaluation specifications; Seed Loom can benchmark its approved authority fixtures against this without copying Microsoft's ontology.
Consultancy implication: an Agent Evaluation & Delivery Control Review can test whether written policy is connected to executable permissions, stop gates, receipts, and independent evaluation.
significance: Directly reinforces the newly approved Seed Loom authority and stop-gate fixtures with a primary-source external benchmark.
assumptions: Microsoft's specification is useful as a benchmark even though it applies only to MAI models.
knownLimitations: The code is draft and aspirational; enforcement effectiveness is unproven.
